name: Integumentary system
description: The skin and its layers, cells and receptors, hair, nails, sweat and oil glands, how the skin controls temperature and protects us, and common disorders. Pictures show the skin, scalp hair and eyebrows to name; BodyParts3D has the skin as one surface, so the layers, glands and nails are text questions.

source.name: Written for Study Buddy. Pictures rendered from BodyParts3D (© The Database Center for Life Science, CC BY-SA 2.1 JP).

questions.prompt: Which organ covers the whole outline in red?
questions.explanation: The body's largest organ, about 1.5 to 2 square metres in an adult and about 15% of the body weight.

figure.alt: The whole skin of the body, seen from behind, in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What does the integumentary system consist of?
answers: Skin, hair, nails and the skin glands
The skin and its appendages: hair, nails, glands
questions.explanation: Together with the receptors in the skin.

figure.alt: The whole skin of the body, seen from behind, in red
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What are the three layers of the skin and tissue under it, from the surface down?
questions.explanation: The hypodermis is strictly not part of the skin.

questions.prompt: Which kind of tissue is the epidermis?
questions.explanation: It has no blood vessels: it is fed from the dermis.

questions.prompt: Which kind of tissue is the dermis mostly made of?
questions.explanation: With collagen and elastic fibres, blood vessels, nerves, glands and hair follicles.

questions.prompt: Which layer under the dermis stores fat and insulates the body?
questions.explanation: It also anchors the skin. Injections under the skin go here.

questions.prompt: What are the five layers of the thick epidermis, from the surface down?
answers: Stratum corneum, lucidum, granulosum, spinosum, basale
questions.explanation: The stratum lucidum is found only in the thick skin of the palms and soles.

questions.prompt: In which epidermal layer do the cells divide to renew the skin?
questions.explanation: Also called the stratum germinativum. The cells take about a month to reach the surface.

questions.prompt: Which layer of the epidermis is the outermost, made of dead flat cells full of keratin?
questions.explanation: It is shed continuously.

questions.prompt: Which tough waterproof protein fills the cells of the outer epidermis, and makes hair and nails?
Which cells make up most of the epidermis?
Which cells in the basal layer make melanin?
questions.explanation: The number of melanocytes is about the same in all people. What differs is how much melanin they make.

questions.prompt: Which pigment protects the cell nuclei from ultraviolet light, and gives skin its brown colour?
questions.explanation: Exposure to sunlight makes the skin make more: a tan.

questions.prompt: Which cells of the epidermis are macrophages that take up germs and start the immune response?
Which cells in the basal layer, linked to nerve endings, help us to feel light touch?
What are the two layers of the dermis?
questions.explanation: The papillary layer has fingerlike dermal papillae that push into the epidermis. They make the fingerprints.

questions.prompt: What causes the pattern of fingerprints?
answers: The ridges of the dermal papillae under the epidermis
questions.explanation: They improve the grip and are unique to each person, even identical twins.

questions.prompt: Which protein in the dermis gives the skin its strength?
questions.explanation: Elastin gives it its stretch. Both are lost with age, which causes wrinkles.

questions.prompt: Which receptors in the skin sense deep pressure and vibration?
questions.explanation: They look like onions. Meissner's corpuscles sense light touch.

questions.prompt: Which receptors in the dermal papillae of the fingertips sense light touch?
Which skin receptors detect pain and temperature?
Where is the skin thickest?
questions.explanation: About 1.5 mm of epidermis there, against 0.1 mm on the eyelids. It has no hair.

questions.prompt: Where is the skin thinnest?
Which structure is highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: Hair is dead keratin. It grows from follicles in the dermis.

figure.alt: The hair of the scalp, in red, over the skull seen from the side
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: Which structures are highlighted in red?
questions.explanation: They keep sweat and rain out of the eyes, and are used to show expression.

figure.alt: The eyebrows, in red, on the head seen from the front
figure.credit: BodyParts3D, © The Database Center for Life Science

questions.prompt: What are the two main parts of a hair?
answers: The shaft above the skin and the root in the follicle
questions.explanation: The root ends in the bulb.

questions.prompt: Which cells at the base of the hair follicle are alive and divide, making the hair grow?
answers: Matrix cells in the hair bulb
questions.explanation: The dermal papilla below it feeds the bulb.

questions.prompt: What gives hair its colour?
answers: Melanin made by melanocytes in the bulb
questions.explanation: Grey hair has lost the melanin.

questions.prompt: Which small muscle attached to a hair follicle makes the hair stand up, causing goose bumps?
questions.explanation: Under sympathetic control. It also squeezes sebum out of the gland.

questions.prompt: What are the three phases of the hair growth cycle?
wrong: Growth, loss and replacement, in random order
questions.explanation: Scalp hairs grow for 2 to 6 years, then rest for about 3 months, and are shed.

questions.prompt: About how fast does scalp hair grow?
About how many scalp hairs do we shed each day?
Which glands, usually opening into hair follicles, make an oily secretion called sebum?
questions.explanation: Sebum keeps hair and skin soft and waterproof, and is mildly antibacterial.

questions.prompt: What is acne caused by?
answers: Blocked and inflamed sebaceous glands and follicles
wrong: Infection of the sweat glands only
questions.explanation: Common in teenagers, when androgens make the glands more active.

questions.prompt: Which sweat glands are found all over the body, open directly on the surface and make watery sweat to cool us?
questions.explanation: Densest on the palms, soles and forehead. About 3 million.

questions.prompt: Which sweat glands, in the armpit and groin, open into hair follicles and become active at puberty?
questions.explanation: Their milky sweat is odourless until bacteria break it down.

questions.prompt: Which modified sweat glands in the ear canal make earwax?
What kind of glands are the mammary glands?
What is the nail's hard visible part called?
questions.explanation: It is made of hard keratin.

questions.prompt: From where does the nail grow?
answers: From the nail matrix at its root
questions.explanation: The pale half-moon, the lunula, is the visible part of the matrix.

questions.prompt: About how fast do fingernails grow?
questions.explanation: Toenails grow about a third as fast. A whole fingernail takes about 6 months to grow out.

questions.prompt: What is the cuticle (eponychium) of the nail?
answers: A fold of skin over the base of the nail plate
The skin fold at the base of the nail
wrong: The tissue under the nail plate

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT a main function of the skin?
wrong: Protecting against germs, water loss and injury
questions.explanation: Red blood cells are made in the bone marrow.

questions.prompt: How does the skin cool the body when it is hot?
answers: The blood vessels widen and the sweat glands make sweat
wrong: The blood vessels narrow and the hairs stand up
questions.explanation: Sweat cools us as it evaporates.

questions.prompt: How does the skin help the body keep warm when it is cold?
answers: The blood vessels narrow and the hairs stand up
wrong: The blood vessels widen and sweat is made
questions.explanation: Shivering of the muscles adds heat.

questions.prompt: Which vitamin does the skin make when it is exposed to sunlight?
questions.explanation: UVB turns a cholesterol derivative into vitamin D3, which the liver and kidney activate.

questions.prompt: Why is the surface of the skin slightly acid, with a pH of about 5?
answers: It slows the growth of bacteria
questions.explanation: Sweat and sebum form the 'acid mantle'.

questions.prompt: Which degree of burn damages the epidermis and the upper dermis, with blisters, and is painful?
questions.explanation: In a first-degree burn only the epidermis is hurt (red, as in sunburn). A third-degree burn goes through the dermis and is often painless, as the nerve endings are destroyed.

questions.prompt: Why is a full-thickness (third-degree) burn often painless?
answers: The nerve endings in the dermis are destroyed
wrong: The pain receptors are in the hypodermis

questions.prompt: What is the 'rule of nines' used for?
answers: To estimate the share of the body surface burned
Estimating the area of a burn
questions.explanation: An adult's head is about 9%, each arm 9%, the front of the trunk 18%, the back 18% and each leg 18%.

questions.prompt: Which skin cancer comes from melanocytes and is the most dangerous?
questions.explanation: It spreads early. The ABCDE signs: asymmetry, border, colour, diameter and evolving.

questions.prompt: Which skin cancer is the most common, rarely spreads, and comes from the basal cells?
questions.explanation: Often appears as a pearly lump with a rolled edge on sun-exposed skin.

questions.prompt: Which chronic condition causes red, scaly plaques as the epidermal cells are made too fast?
questions.explanation: An autoimmune disease.

questions.prompt: What is the term for an itchy inflamed skin often linked to allergy and asthma?
What is the usual order of events in healing a skin wound?
answers: Bleeding and clotting, inflammation, new tissue grows, scar remodelling

questions.prompt: What is a scar mostly made of?
questions.explanation: It has no hair follicles or glands.

questions.prompt: What causes a pressure ulcer (bedsore)?
answers: Long pressure cutting off the blood supply to the skin
Pressure that blocks blood flow to the skin
questions.explanation: Typically over bony areas such as the sacrum and heels.

questions.prompt: Which part of sunlight does most of the damage that causes sunburn and skin cancer?
questions.explanation: UVB burns the skin; UVA penetrates deeper and ages it.

questions.prompt: What is the term for a yellow colour of the skin, from too much bilirubin?
What is a blue colour of the skin from a lack of oxygen in the blood called?
What is redness of the skin, from widened blood vessels, called?
What is albinism?
answers: A lack of melanin, from a gene fault
An inherited lack of melanin production
questions.explanation: Melanocytes are present, but cannot make melanin.
